**Agile** and **Waterfall** are two fundamental project management methodologies with `opposite approaches to structure, planning, and delivery`.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF1-5U6iRaPMumMelVb6c7J3EtBW7wxRKKbxwDU9heejBrfsEmF6mMOew_vQpYhFcz2I8Q2zCY17NcC3czryl2BQdnP93JJOzFvr654g0sos21_x1d5MxwRmyTncF4AYy8Xyas0skXS4b7PFP7ameyS42-lwXQcOLCSCqXUc17SyxqcEj_ug)

### Waterfall

- **Structure:** Linear and sequential. Projects move step-by-step through distinct phases—such as Requirements, Design, Implementation, Verification, and Maintenance—where each stage must finish completely before the next begins.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScAHEIkXXj-IIa92GujcH0Oo7DGo-gCX4w4O_N0Num-4vvqbVH2r9j-78-ldNNpSa63K5buyYFuWafoUn26yPVsUOPKwU58k7t3aEoJyGL8FO9VC6nXj-3B6KFm4V_axZojDBBvyavFcsHEpXXMi6Bpw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF1-5U6iRaPMumMelVb6c7J3EtBW7wxRKKbxwDU9heejBrfsEmF6mMOew_vQpYhFcz2I8Q2zCY17NcC3czryl2BQdnP93JJOzFvr654g0sos21_x1d5MxwRmyTncF4AYy8Xyas0skXS4b7PFP7ameyS42-lwXQcOLCSCqXUc17SyxqcEj_ug)
- **Planning:** Heavy, front-loaded planning. Scope, budget, and requirements are locked in early.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScgHEIkXXG_u8Li6WTcKM0J2Sg9yZ-5bDMg_he8AeM7Ib3lXJIz14nlIEbekfdgN4S4ec7TilVhWIEm7XuA_kZ0cOqeacfPuODwQUzyLky3uIFkyDiB3ntHcd8KulBKA9skfNK5EeWmcyXVcGZnbn1ERVjQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnwEBxCJF1-EXRXTakCcWbuTIKPqnJt3V3eZOeEOH_ukEVo0ERKYUnERJMBEbJ3QBOkFt9Xuq3v_03XIsqYzYpcErIzRgzWSW4jaGEl2y8DOIVYKlN0F0nkZz_GXmXhKfjVISo2oCr7PHqRrUSewyke3tiAE-2rQmMmqSD6uZ-wdqFV3jUOk6j5cBjQSzGuxevCMI2VV-l8SJDg_AisURiYQ)
- **Flexibility:** Low. Changes mid-project are difficult and costly because going back a phase breaks the sequence.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/7vBPfGIg2EY)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnwEBxCJF1-EXRXTakCcWbuTIKPqnJt3V3eZOeEOH_ukEVo0ERKYUnERJMBEbJ3QBOkFt9Xuq3v_03XIsqYzYpcErIzRgzWSW4jaGEl2y8DOIVYKlN0F0nkZz_GXmXhKfjVISo2oCr7PHqRrUSewyke3tiAE-2rQmMmqSD6uZ-wdqFV3jUOk6j5cBjQSzGuxevCMI2VV-l8SJDg_AisURiYQ)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BGzeDcFZPVc&t=67)
- **Customer Involvement:** Low after initial planning; the client usually sees the final product at the very end ("big bang" delivery).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESngEBxCJF119S5JjVtBs1qYWIKbr8tL5CsBy5EJFHWZZntaqp1llJXJ7TL-gUovw3PoPlHL5oWKTQj0nCBdMMamV2rS-X3iQGaND0kVWZx_3D9yWMUCsG6g01ystG_I0ahFQS7ZeaUuI-TiMc4CW142bo4laQDxjSAHG2y_dNkjQFeWfqh-PD_n0qCg0C919ObEYGo68Z6zvbF8GR739Mmw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeQHEIkXXcBmiH_rmFmZXmjPoXXfqUfrXz1o0S5G6IgUobG6mVl-EXLDdsuDwxJ8q_A_oD1kTJGL2xCKdrUxwR_6wyrT5wkyzbAxTc7OWik_zYx8FoldPs0WW_gaDTws_GQDUdu6ZQiR4BIk4CU1huRBMixWG5_rO2gs)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U28U5QXs4jk&t=10)
- **Best Used For:** Projects with fixed, well-understood requirements, regulatory/compliance needs, or physical construction where changes are rare and expensive.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U28U5QXs4jk&t=10)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScgHEIkXXG_u8Li6WTcKM0J2Sg9yZ-5bDMg_he8AeM7Ib3lXJIz14nlIEbekfdgN4S4ec7TilVhWIEm7XuA_kZ0cOqeacfPuODwQUzyLky3uIFkyDiB3ntHcd8KulBKA9skfNK5EeWmcyXVcGZnbn1ERVjQ)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESogEBxCJF19sK1PbXfPtrAXpFzm5KCWQLz7HwudhKyJh_AHPskMikPKjGpCEHPDmLHOqUWq0ceo6n0n_klW0rxz3-aIYdYlSe0AqnF8w4JuoTEcrRPn3cF08ucsvnFQ5MhxJwC_wL2sohSrUmWXttSYweNdN0qx34NFy4y4g6W1JbmfDvaNKxRRyKt-jAWCghmeEXqN9s_L384ciKVvv83mrMDCI)
- **Learn More:** Review structured guidance from [IBM](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScAHEIkXXj-IIa92GujcH0Oo7DGo-gCX4w4O_N0Num-4vvqbVH2r9j-78-ldNNpSa63K5buyYFuWafoUn26yPVsUOPKwU58k7t3aEoJyGL8FO9VC6nXj-3B6KFm4V_axZojDBBvyavFcsHEpXXMi6Bpw) or the [Project Management Institute](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkgEBxCJF1wHpxxlsx__Xj09yf1L7mYP_NlpN5j8U8CJtIGV06w_ND8Pylo428yBZ3AbMMAEi3TKEhVht2IsMsOKXHR3ZyHSrLsyFc09KsC8LoAbfygheWs8gbT4x_3PiZ3W4MKkO4bEYq-3MkBYXzq_DpBg14tBDGitgOcEhimGlOYATnuVKGvky2H7tGQwyOU2iyw).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScAHEIkXXj-IIa92GujcH0Oo7DGo-gCX4w4O_N0Num-4vvqbVH2r9j-78-ldNNpSa63K5buyYFuWafoUn26yPVsUOPKwU58k7t3aEoJyGL8FO9VC6nXj-3B6KFm4V_axZojDBBvyavFcsHEpXXMi6Bpw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkgEBxCJF1wHpxxlsx__Xj09yf1L7mYP_NlpN5j8U8CJtIGV06w_ND8Pylo428yBZ3AbMMAEi3TKEhVht2IsMsOKXHR3ZyHSrLsyFc09KsC8LoAbfygheWs8gbT4x_3PiZ3W4MKkO4bEYq-3MkBYXzq_DpBg14tBDGitgOcEhimGlOYATnuVKGvky2H7tGQwyOU2iyw)

### Agile

- **Structure:** Iterative and incremental. Work is broken down into short, repeating cycles called "sprints" (usually 2 to 4 weeks).
- **Planning:** Adaptive and flexible. Requirements and solutions evolve through continuous collaboration.
- **Flexibility:** High. Scope can shift at the start of each new sprint based on feedback.
- **Customer Involvement:** High and continuous. Stakeholders review working increments of the product after every sprint.
- **Best Used For:** Dynamic projects where goals are unclear at the start, fast time-to-market is critical, or software development is ongoing.
- **Learn More:** Explore workflows on [Atlassian](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF11VOJT0iadU_dmQ_YZ1W7KJbiH7jlzL3hutiLjf85wd_F9Q3hpaY2fO12460DbRXN1cej69gWBSosNs7dECCD56ayzj4RWEKfpuZJc2NrIHWRc8Sa9BiBxz1MSG4oaQc5TGWeRCGPd0x3uoah7lhsZK14EWq1o65pEZ318tvZE9NH6XP).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF1-5U6iRaPMumMelVb6c7J3EtBW7wxRKKbxwDU9heejBrfsEmF6mMOew_vQpYhFcz2I8Q2zCY17NcC3czryl2BQdnP93JJOzFvr654g0sos21_x1d5MxwRmyTncF4AYy8Xyas0skXS4b7PFP7ameyS42-lwXQcOLCSCqXUc17SyxqcEj_ug)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScAHEIkXXj-IIa92GujcH0Oo7DGo-gCX4w4O_N0Num-4vvqbVH2r9j-78-ldNNpSa63K5buyYFuWafoUn26yPVsUOPKwU58k7t3aEoJyGL8FO9VC6nXj-3B6KFm4V_axZojDBBvyavFcsHEpXXMi6Bpw)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qf0Yzrzr_i4&vl=en&t=25)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeQHEIkXXcBmiH_rmFmZXmjPoXXfqUfrXz1o0S5G6IgUobG6mVl-EXLDdsuDwxJ8q_A_oD1kTJGL2xCKdrUxwR_6wyrT5wkyzbAxTc7OWik_zYx8FoldPs0WW_gaDTws_GQDUdu6ZQiR4BIk4CU1huRBMixWG5_rO2gs)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnwEBxCJF1-EXRXTakCcWbuTIKPqnJt3V3eZOeEOH_ukEVo0ERKYUnERJMBEbJ3QBOkFt9Xuq3v_03XIsqYzYpcErIzRgzWSW4jaGEl2y8DOIVYKlN0F0nkZz_GXmXhKfjVISo2oCr7PHqRrUSewyke3tiAE-2rQmMmqSD6uZ-wdqFV3jUOk6j5cBjQSzGuxevCMI2VV-l8SJDg_AisURiYQ)[[6]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/7vBPfGIg2EY)[[7]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BGzeDcFZPVc&t=67)[[8]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U28U5QXs4jk&t=10)[[9]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF11VOJT0iadU_dmQ_YZ1W7KJbiH7jlzL3hutiLjf85wd_F9Q3hpaY2fO12460DbRXN1cej69gWBSosNs7dECCD56ayzj4RWEKfpuZJc2NrIHWRc8Sa9BiBxz1MSG4oaQc5TGWeRCGPd0x3uoah7lhsZK14EWq1o65pEZ318tvZE9NH6XP)

### Key Comparison
| Feature | Waterfall | Agile |
|---|---|---|
| **Approach** | Linear & sequential | Iterative & incremental |
| **Change Management** | Rigid; hard to change once started | Fluid; welcomes changing requirements |
| **Delivery** | Single final release at the end | Continuous, smaller releases |
| **Documentation** | Extensive and comprehensive | Light; focuses on working output |

### Hybrid Approach
Many organizations combine both methods (often called **Hybrid**, **Wagile** , or **Water-Scrum-Fall** ) by using Waterfall for upfront budgeting, compliance, and core architecture, while using Agile for product design and feature delivery.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESogEBxCJF19sK1PbXfPtrAXpFzm5KCWQLz7HwudhKyJh_AHPskMikPKjGpCEHPDmLHOqUWq0ceo6n0n_klW0rxz3-aIYdYlSe0AqnF8w4JuoTEcrRPn3cF08ucsvnFQ5MhxJwC_wL2sohSrUmWXttSYweNdN0qx34NFy4y4g6W1JbmfDvaNKxRRyKt-jAWCghmeEXqN9s_L384ciKVvv83mrMDCI)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScgHEIkXXG_u8Li6WTcKM0J2Sg9yZ-5bDMg_he8AeM7Ib3lXJIz14nlIEbekfdgN4S4ec7TilVhWIEm7XuA_kZ0cOqeacfPuODwQUzyLky3uIFkyDiB3ntHcd8KulBKA9skfNK5EeWmcyXVcGZnbn1ERVjQ)Are you trying to decide on a methodology for a **specific project** (like software development, marketing, or construction)? items.title: Key Comparison
items.text:
Feature Waterfall Agile
Approach Linear & sequential Iterative & incremental
Change Management Rigid; hard to change once started Fluid; welcomes changing requirements
Delivery Single final release at the end Continuous, smaller releases
Documentation Extensive and comprehensive Light; focuses on working output
items.markdown:
| Feature | Waterfall | Agile |
|---|---|---|
| **Approach** | Linear & sequential | Iterative & incremental |
| **Change Management** | Rigid; hard to change once started | Fluid; welcomes changing requirements |
| **Delivery** | Single final release at the end | Continuous, smaller releases |
| **Documentation** | Extensive and comprehensive | Light; focuses on working output |

items.title: Hybrid Approach
items.text: Many organizations combine both methods (often called Hybrid, Wagile, or Water-Scrum-Fall ) by using Waterfall for upfront budgeting, compliance, and core architecture, while using Agile for product design and feature delivery.
